972.headline: What's actually left to win

975.body:
The most common win left on "$1,000,000 Money Rush" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and four of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything here about "$1,000,000 Money Rush" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 14.
975.headline: The prize table, line by line

976.body:

If "100X The Cash" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
976.headline: Top prize already claimed

980.body:
"20X The Cash" has had no $250,000 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of 20X The Cash's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
980.headline: No top prize claimed lately

981.body:
"50X The Cash" is close to selling out, with only a small slice of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Every line of 50X The Cash's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
981.headline: Tickets sold so far

985.body:
"MAX-A-MILLION" has gone three months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $1 million prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

For "MAX-A-MILLION" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

Today's free summary of "MAX-A-MILLION" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
